prompt: The single most dramatic moment of a calm ink-and-wash world-conquest board game: an attack across a border. Top-down-ish board view, tighter than full map, centered on two adjacent territories (a sage green one attacking a vermilion one). A single confident gold brush stroke sweeps from the attacker across the border, tapering and splitting into dry-brush bristle marks at its tip. Three small bone-white dice with dark pips have just landed in a quiet translucent tray at the lower edge of the frame. On the defending territory, a pale ivory brush-painted soldier figure is dissolving upward into wisps of ink smoke. The rest of the board is dimmed and still, indigo paper, silver ink coastlines, muted washes as in the first reference; figures as in the second. One gold only: the stroke. Tension through restraint, not explosions: no fire, no sparks, no glow bloom, no text, no kanji, no seals, no blossoms, no UI buttons.
